comments.body:
=== SESSION: e369 Jira DC — the certification trap ruled on and fixed; five children in review; nothing landable ===

--- THE BLOCKER THAT DOMINATES EVERYTHING ---
`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` is **803 LOC on gerrit/main**, over the LOCKED 800 cap.
The module-size gate scans every `src/rebar` file, so **no change in the repo can earn `Verified +1`**
until it is split. I did not touch that file's size; it crossed the cap in `339262b990 (af11)`. The
operator confirmed another session owns the split. Everything below is pushed and waiting on it.

Second, separate CI failure, and it WAS mine: the **comment-hygiene gate**. A bare CI run id in a
docstring is a rot-prone reference; the guard wants a resolvable ticket id. My fix for it landed in a
LATER commit of the stack, so changes 1370/1371 kept failing while 1372+ passed. **Gerrit tests each
patchset independently — verifying only the stack tip proves nothing about its ancestors.** Rebuilt
the stack so the fix sits in the commit that introduced the violation, then verified hygiene + ruff
on EACH of the five commits separately.

--- MERGED (2) ---
  1361  1019  clamp max_tokens to the model being called   (restored the verifier's sight)
  1359  4b9e  the Epic Link clear probe

--- IN REVIEW (8), all blocked on the module-size gate ---
  1370 d582  collision-free rekey target        1378 738a  attest a disposition close
  1371 275e  non-admin application-properties   1380 2bc7  guard 2 shared-key loaders
  1372 59b2  let the vacuous assertions fail    1381 2e47  assert issue-type names unambiguous
  1373 4b9e  keep probe evidence on setup fail  1375 2e47  vocabulary decisions as data

--- THE CERTIFICATION TRAP: two correct rules, no honest exit ---
The close path exempts a `duplicate`/`not_a_bug`/`escalated` bug naming a live replacement from
completion verification — right, since it never claimed to implement its own ACs. But it returned no
sign signal, and `child_closure_findings` counts ANY unsigned closure as uncertified, withholding the
parent's signature. Reopening took the same exemption every time; `--force-close` produced exactly
the state the ruling forbids.

**The exemption keyed on the link that DOCUMENTS the disposition:**

    disposition closes WITH a live replacement link  ->  7 of 7 UNSIGNED
    disposition closes WITHOUT one                   ->  7 CERTIFIED

So certification was reachable only for duplicates that HID their replacement. Operator ruled: attest
them. Implemented (1378) — deterministic, no LLM call, and the manifest says
`completion-verifier: DISPOSITION duplicate` + the replacement id rather than a `PASS` that never
happened. Verified end to end: 0059 is now `certified`, and e369's uncertified count fell 2 -> 1.

--- WHO FORCED AND WHO DID NOT: the earlier reopen conflated two tickets ---
The reopen rationale said 0059 and 2bc7 both "closed WITHOUT a completion-verifier attestation … so
it never passed the gate". **True for 2bc7, FALSE for 0059.**

    0059  FORCE_CLOSE records: 0   class=duplicate     took the sanctioned exemption
    2bc7  FORCE_CLOSE records: 1   class=preexisting   an agent bypassing the gate

`preexisting` is not a disposition class, so 2bc7 genuinely owed verification, could not satisfy the
referencing-commit precheck (its fix landed under J4's commit naming 0a94), and was forced.

**I first inferred "not forced" from the STATUS event lacking a force field. That was wrong** —
force-close is recorded as an audit COMMENT, never in the event, so a forced and an unforced close
leave identical event keys. The comment is the only discriminator.

--- METHOD: three scans lied to me before one told the truth ---
1. **A regex scan reported "109 unguarded loaders". Artifact.** My function-body regex matched
   `(.*?)\):` for the arg list, which mis-parses every `def f(...) -> Type:`. The AST pass gave 4 of
   213 cache-first. I discarded the regex number rather than reporting it.
2. **Two force-close scans returned ZERO** — one pointed at a tracker copy lacking the records, one
   used `subprocess` `grep`, which disagreed with the shell's (193 files vs 0). Only pure Python was
   trustworthy. An empty result is not evidence of absence until the scan itself is checked.
3. **I published an audit table with a wrong row** and corrected it: `test_mutation.py` does not
   overwrite `sys.modules`, it returns an UNREGISTERED private copy — which is literally 2bc7's
   title, so that helper is one cross-file `isinstance` from reproducing the bug. Safe by
   circumstance, not construction.

--- THE LABEL-LIMIT TRAP THE EPIC'S OWN ORACLES CAUGHT ---
DC rejects a 255-char label and accepts 254, so I tightened the shared constant. **Four
characterization oracles went red.** `sanitize_label` RAISES above the ceiling rather than
truncating, so a shared 254 makes the live-validated CLOUD path reject a label Cloud accepts —
trading a silent DC defect for a loud Cloud regression, the exact risk this epic was built to avoid.
Reverted; the fix is a per-deployment ceiling on 049e's `comment_max_chars` precedent. The oracles
did their job on me.

--- THE PROBE ANSWERED NOTHING, AND DESTROYED THE EVIDENCE OF WHY ---
Run 30930839323: `PROBE SETUP FAILED: Epic Link=None Epic Name=None`, then
`No files were found with the provided path`. Evidence was written only after the LAST question while
every setup-failure path raises `SystemExit` — so the one artifact built to explain a failure was
guaranteed to be discarded exactly when needed. On an amd64-only image each attempt costs a full boot,
which makes an undiagnosable failure the expensive kind. Fixed (1373). **4b9e's blocking unknown is
still OPEN and the Rank 1 cell stays unwritten.**

Constraint 1 refined: a `workflow_dispatch` file must exist on the DEFAULT branch to be dispatchable,
but once it does, `--ref` may target any ref — so the landing cost is per-workflow, not per-iteration.

--- FILED THIS SESSION ---
  738a  the certification trap (FIXED, 1378)
  502b  6 tickets carry a FORCE_CLOSE record AND a certified attestation — OBSERVATION, not diagnosed;
        the trusted op-cert gate service is the leading unverified hypothesis. `e95e` is signed BEFORE
        its force-close, which that hypothesis does not explain.
  e351  209 of 213 by-path loaders are not cache-first, on keys shared by up to 9 files

--- STATE HANDED OVER ---
 * epic e369 in_progress, claimed. **AC4 still UNTICKED** — the live harness run at current main
   (30933704255) is the evidence, dispatched per the operator's restatement that real DC sync
   demonstrated by the live CI environment is the load-bearing requirement.
 * e369 uncertified: 1 (b586, `stale-material` — remediable by re-closing).
 * 0059 CLOSED + certified. 2bc7 / 2e47 / 275e / 59b2 / d582 still OPEN — deliberately: their changes
   are not `Verified +1`, and 2e47 has two genuinely unmet ACs (the per-deployment label ceiling and
   the duplicate-`Task` resolution).
 * Nothing closed to unblock the epic. Every close waits on green CI.

comments.body:
=== SESSION: e369 Jira DC — 12 changes landed, AC4 attested, and four gate defects found by using the gates ===

--- OUTCOME ---
Epic e369: **all 13 ACs met (AC4 attested), 0 uncertified descendants, 3 open children.** 12 Gerrit
changes merged, each with `Verified +1` + `LLM-Review +1`. Five tickets closed AND certified: 0059,
2bc7, d582, 275e, 59b2.

--- THE OPERATOR RULINGS THAT SHAPED IT ---
1. **"operator-attested just means not code-verifiable"** — I had been refusing to tick AC4, treating
   `[operator-attested]` as requiring a human. It marks criteria a test cannot check. Attested AC4 on
   run 30933704255 with both bidirectional cells named, and d582's AC via the route its own text offered.
2. **"attest duplicates with a live link"** — settled the certification trap below.
3. **"once deleted in Jira, it shouldn't be resurrected"** — settled 3b5f, and widened it: rebar
   resurrects TODAY on a 3-pass delay, through a path no ticket had examined.
4. **"if Cloud and DC both fail, they are both deficient"** — corrected my framing that symmetry was
   exculpatory. It is two deficiencies, not zero.

--- FOUR GATE DEFECTS, ALL FOUND BY USING THE GATES ---
* **738a** (FIXED, 1378) — the certification trap. The close path exempts a disposition from completion
  verification; the certification path demands an attestation from every closed child. Composed into a
  state with no honest exit. Measured: **7 of 7 disposition closes WITH a live link were unsigned; 7
  WITHOUT one were certified** — certification was reachable only for duplicates that HID their
  replacement. Now mints an honest `DISPOSITION` manifest, never a `PASS` it did not earn. `--force-close`
  stays unsigned, mutation-checked.
* **3787** (P1) — Rebase-If-Necessary submits a tree CI never validated. `main` violated the LOCKED
  800-LOC cap while every landed change was green: change 1367's tested patchset had the file at 800, its
  merged commit at 803. No administrator overrode anything.
* **ab54 / 7084** — a PASS `COMPLETION_VERDICT` sidecar is silently lost on lock contention (swallowed
  twice, no retry, exit 0), amplified by compact-on-close holding the store lock for a measured **2m17s**.
  And these "isolated" worktrees are **symlinks to one store** — same lock inode. My isolation assumption
  was wrong all session.
* **9790** (FIXED, 1387) — `serverInfo` 200 is not readiness for Jira Software custom fields. Measured:
  green after 8m32s, and one second later the inventory was 27 fields, **all system**, no
  `customfield_*`. The harness shares the identical gate and only survives because it is slower afterwards.
* **6a81** (FIXED, 1388) — `recheck-review` refused a `bugfix-size-attestation` block even once attested,
  and a no-code-change patchset copies the -1 forward. The remedy there is a TICKET action, so
  amend+re-push was the wrong instruction.
* **df3a** (P1, OPEN) — the completion verifier returns a dependency-link record where a
  `CompletionVerdict` belongs. Blocks b586. A `/rebar-debug` subagent is root-causing it.

--- MEASUREMENT BEAT DOCUMENTATION, TWICE ---
* **The capability map was WRONG.** req-0071/0072/0073 recorded DC rejecting a 255-char label. The live
  cell measured **255 accepted and read back**. No Cloud/DC divergence; the shared constant was right all
  along. Retracted with the run id (1389). I had already declined to tighten the constant — correctly, but
  for the weaker reason (Cloud regression) rather than the real one (the premise was false).
* **049e's documentary claim was RIGHT**, now measured: both application-properties paths return 403 to a
  non-admin PAT and 200 to admin. The admin leg is what makes it conclusive — 403-beside-200 is "present
  but privileged", not "absent".

--- MY OWN ERRORS, EACH CAUGHT BY A CHECK I NEARLY SKIPPED ---
1. **I tightened a shared constant and four characterization oracles went red.** `sanitize_label` RAISES
   rather than truncates, so a shared 254 would make Cloud reject what Cloud accepts. The oracles did
   their job on me.
2. **An edit cut 3b5f's description at the first `## Acceptance criteria`** and silently discarded the
   whole Plan section I had appended after it. Two of `review-plan`'s three findings were accurate reports
   of that mangled text — and I was about to dismiss one as a staleness artifact.
3. **I passed along an inherited citation without checking it.** b9b8 did NOT rework the probe cell as its
   scope — but the rename DID ride b9b8's commit (`ae009443a9`). Both the ticket and the reviewer were
   half right. **Third instance this epic of work bundled into an unrelated ticket's commit.**
4. **`make lint` covers only `src tests`.** I left `_FIELD_POLL_INTERVAL_S` undefined in `scripts/`; CI
   would not have caught it. Then my blind line-wrapper wrapped inside an f-string and broke the file.
5. **I trusted my own echo instead of the command's output** — twice. `rebar edit --parent` refuses a
   closed parent, and zsh does not word-split unquoted `$f`, so two "posted" comments never existed.
6. **I reported "all 10 local failures were the ddgs dep" having seen only 4** — my command captured the
   last 5 lines.
7. **`recheck` vs `recheck-review`** are different triggers. My blanket `recheck` neither cleared the
   review vote nor left CI alone — the cancellations posted `Verified -1`, which I then reported to the
   operator as CI failures.

--- b586: THE STALE SIGNATURE WAS THE SMALL PROBLEM ---
Verifying its criteria BEFORE reopening (rather than after) found it had closed with five unchecked ACs,
two factually false: it claimed two children and had **zero**. S1 `f2f3` and S2 `6758` were closed,
certified, and sitting at `parent_id = ''` — orphans the epic never counted. Re-parented rather than
amending the criteria to match the miss. Then the close hit df3a and I did NOT force past it.

--- STATE HANDED OVER ---
* `2e47` — 2 ACs, both answered by dispatched harness run **30951453979** (`d394a7052`).
* `3b5f` — implemented, **Gerrit 1393** (522+/1153-), awaiting both gates. Four judgement calls flagged
  for review on the ticket. NOT verified by me, NOT closed.
* `b586` — one well-formed verdict from closing; blocked on df3a. Do NOT `--force-close`.
* Filed and open: 3787, ab54, 7084, df3a, e351, 502b, 2c93 (largely moot), 738a-follow-ups, f020.
